title: From Financial Constraints to Educational Aspirations: How Scholarship Support Helped Ganesh Kumar Pursue His B.Tech Education
body_text:
Higher education can create opportunities for young people to build meaningful careers and work towards a stable and independent future. However, financial constraints can make it difficult for students from economically weaker families to meet the costs associated with higher education.
Demonstrating the importance of educational financial assistance, Ganesh Kumar, a 21-year-old B.Tech. II Year student from the OBC-NCL category, has been able to continue his education with scholarship support of ₹ 87,000/- provided in 2026 .
Coming from a family facing financial constraints, Ganesh Kumar faced difficulties in managing the expenses associated with his education. The economic barrier made it challenging for his family to bear the educational expenses required for his continued studies.
Despite these difficulties, Ganesh remained focused on his education and aspired to complete his higher education. His determination to continue his academic journey helped him remain focused on pursuing his B.Tech. education.
Reducing Financial Burden and Strengthening Educational Aspirations
Scholarship assistance of ₹ 87,000/- provided in 2026 helped Ganesh Kumar meet his educational expenses. The support reduced the financial burden on his family and helped him continue his education.
The financial assistance provided relief to his family from the expenses associated with his education and enabled Ganesh to continue pursuing his B.Tech. studies.
Currently, Ganesh Kumar is pursuing his B.Tech. II Year and continuing his academic journey. The scholarship support has helped reduce the educational expenses borne by his family and supported him in overcoming the economic barrier faced by his family.
With continued determination and the support received through the scholarship, Ganesh Kumar is working towards completing his higher education. His journey illustrates how timely educational assistance can help students from financially constrained families overcome economic barriers and pursue their academic aspirations.
By supporting his educational expenses, the scholarship has helped Ganesh Kumar continue his academic journey and move closer to his aspiration of completing higher education.
SS-25-TAR-KV-GA

enrichment.summary: This PIB release profiles Ganesh Kumar, a 21-year-old B.Tech II Year student from the OBC-NCL (Non-Creamy Layer) category, who received ₹87,000 in scholarship support in 2026 under a Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment scheme. The financial assistance helped reduce the economic burden on his family and enabled him to continue his higher education despite financial constraints.
enrichment.context:
The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment administers several post-matric and pre-matric scholarship schemes for socially and educationally backward classes, including OBCs, to reduce dropout rates and promote access to higher education. The 'Non-Creamy Layer' (NCL) criterion, established following the Indra Sawhney judgment (1992), excludes economically advanced sections of OBCs from reservation and welfare benefits, ensuring that assistance reaches genuinely disadvantaged families. Scholarships such as the Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC students are typically routed through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) using Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to ensure transparency and timely disbursal.

Such beneficiary-story releases are part of the government's broader communication strategy to showcase the real-world impact of welfare schemes, often tied to initiatives highlighting last-mile delivery of social justice programmes. While this specific release is largely anecdotal, it reflects the functioning of OBC welfare architecture, an important area for understanding India's social justice and affirmative action framework relevant to governance and social empowerment topics in the UPSC syllabus.

prelims_questions.question: The term 'Non-Creamy Layer' (NCL), often used in the context of OBC reservations and scholarships in India, arose primarily from which of the following?
options: The Indra Sawhney vs Union of India judgment (1992)
The National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993
prelims_questions.explanation: The Supreme Court's judgment in Indra Sawhney vs Union of India (1992) introduced the 'creamy layer' concept to exclude the socially advanced sections among OBCs from reservation benefits, ensuring that welfare measures like scholarships target genuinely disadvantaged individuals.

prelims_questions.question: Scholarships for OBC and other backward class students in India are typically disbursed through which digital platform using Direct Benefit Transfer?
prelims_questions.explanation: The National Scholarship Portal (NSP) is the common platform used by various ministries, including Social Justice & Empowerment, to process and disburse scholarships to eligible students via Direct Benefit Transfer.
